File.title: File
File.description: Represents a single PDF or other document file uploaded by a user or generated as an output of an operation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the File entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who uploaded or owns this file. (Relationship: User 1:N File)

originalFileName.description: The original name of the file when it was uploaded by the user.

storagePath.description: The URI or path indicating where the file is physically stored in the backend (e.g., cloud storage URL, internal file system path).

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document').

fileSize.description: The size of the file in bytes.

uploadDate.description: The timestamp when the file was first uploaded or created in the system.

isOutput.description: A boolean flag indicating if this file is an output generated by a processing operation (true) or an initial user upload (false).

thumbnailUrl.description: An optional URL to a generated thumbnail image for PDF files, useful for UI previews.

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description: Tracks a single PDF processing task initiated by a user, such as merging, splitting, converting, or AI analysis.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Operation entity.

userId.description: Reference to the user who initiated this operation. (Relationship: User 1:N Operation)

operationType.description: The type of PDF operation performed (e.g., 'MERGE', 'SPLIT', 'CONVERT_PDF_TO_WORD', 'CONVERT_WORD_TO_PDF', 'AI_SUMMARY').

status.description: The current status of the operation (e.g., 'PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'COMPLETED', 'FAILED').

requestedAt.description: The timestamp when the operation was initiated by the user.

completedAt.description: The timestamp when the operation was completed. Null if still in progress or failed.

inputFilesIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities that were used as input for this operation. (Relationship: Operation N:N File)

outputFilesIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities that were generated as output by this operation. (Relationship: Operation N:N File)

errorMessage.description: Details about the error if the operation failed, providing context for debugging or user feedback.

AIAnalysisResult.title: AIAnalysisResult
AIAnalysisResult.description: Stores the textual content generated by an AI content analysis tool for a specific PDF document.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AIAnalysisResult entity.

operationId.description: Reference to the Operation entity that performed this AI analysis. (Relationship: Operation 1:N AIAnalysisResult)

sourceFileId.description: Reference to the specific File entity that was analyzed by the AI tool. (Relationship: File 1:N AIAnalysisResult)

analysisType.description: The type of AI analysis performed (e.g., 'SUMMARY', 'KEY_POINTS', 'ENTITY_EXTRACTION').

analysisContent.description: The actual textual result of the AI analysis, such as the document summary or extracted key points.

generatedAt.description: The timestamp when this AI analysis result was generated.

definition.description: Stores individual PDF or document files uploaded by or generated for a specific user. Each document explicitly includes the 'userId' field, which is denormalized for authorization independence. The path's '{userId}' wildcard must match both 'request.auth.uid' and the document's 'userId' field.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this file.

params.name: fileId
params.description: The unique identifier of the file.

definition.description: Tracks PDF processing tasks initiated by a specific user. Each document explicitly includes the 'userId' field, which is denormalized for authorization independence. The path's '{userId}' wildcard must match both 'request.auth.uid' and the document's 'userId' field.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who initiated this operation.

params.name: operationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the operation.

definition.description: Stores AI analysis results for a specific operation performed by a user. To ensure Authorization Independence (Mandate A), this document *must* include a denormalized 'userId' field, matching the parent operation's owner. The path's '{userId}' wildcard must match both 'request.auth.uid' and the document's 'userId' field.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent operation and this AI analysis result.

params.name: operationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent operation that generated this AI analysis result.

params.name: aiAnalysisResultId
params.description: The unique identifier of the AI analysis result.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for PDF Spark prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles and mandates. The central theme is user-centric data partitioning, where all user-specific documents (Files, Operations, AI Analysis Results) are nested under a `/users/{userId}` path. This approach ensures robust authorization independence and simplifies security rules.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
This design achieves authorization independence by:
1.  **Path-Based Ownership:** All private user data is directly nested under `/users/{userId}`. This means that for any document at paths like `/users/{userId}/files/{fileId}`, the `userId` is immediately available in the `request.path` in security rules (`request.resource.path[1]`).
2.  **Denormalization:** For `File` and `Operation` entities, the `userId` field is already present in their schemas. This `userId` field within the document will explicitly match the `userId` in the path and `request.auth.uid`. For `AIAnalysisResult` documents, which are nested under operations, we mandate including a `userId` field directly within the `AIAnalysisResult` document. This denormalization ensures that a security rule can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with the document's `userId` field and the path's `userId` wildcard (e.g., `match /users/{userId}/operations/{operationId}/aiAnalysisResults/{aiAnalysisResultId} { allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId && resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid; }`), without needing to perform a `get()` operation on a parent `Operation` document to determine ownership. This entirely eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies, making transactions and batch writes atomic and rules far easier to reason about and debug.

**QAPs (Secure List Operations):**
The structure inherently supports secure `list` operations (Query as a Proxy for Security - QAPs) by leveraging structural segregation and path-based ownership:
1.  **Homogeneous Security Posture:** Each collection (`/users/{userId}/files`, `/users/{userId}/operations`, `/users/{userId}/operations/{operationId}/aiAnalysisResults`) holds documents that share the exact same authorization requirements: they are owned by the user specified in the `{userId}` wildcard of the path. There is no mixing of public and private data or different access levels within the same collection.
2.  **Direct Path Validation:** Security rules can directly enforce `request.auth.uid == userId` for `list` operations on these collections. For example, a user listing files from `/users/{current_user_id}/files` will only be able to retrieve documents where the path's `userId` matches their authenticated UID. This means the client-side queries do not need to filter by `userId`; the security rules act as the definitive filter, ensuring that only data the user is authorized to see is returned, even if a malicious client attempts to bypass filters.

This design ensures that authorization is explicit, atomic, and easy to verify, significantly reducing the surface area for security vulnerabilities and simplifying rule development and debugging.
